principles: Only fix real experimental correctness and traceability issues.
Keep host-neutral boundaries: host/adaptor names must not stand in for model-family evidence.
Prefer lightweight deterministic readiness artifacts over provider calls or large experiments.
Research evidence remains separate from product gates, playbooks, runtime memory, and DONE policy.
drivers: M0 must make Phase 1 safe to start later without spending tokens now.
The protocol must prevent mixed-factor comparisons and post-hoc runner inclusion.
The artifacts must be readable and verifiable by future Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, or other hosts.

options.name: docs-and-examples-only
pros: No provider calls or experimental spend
Enough to freeze runner/cell/budget semantics before Phase 1
cons: Does not automatically validate manifests beyond documented checks
Future story may need scripts if the process becomes frequent

options.name: full-readiness-tooling-now
pros: Could mechanically validate manifests and locks from day one
cons: Adds code surface before the need is proven
Risks optimizing tooling before any real Phase 1 execution

options.name: start-phase1-immediately
cons: Can waste tokens before harness/tool/budget readiness is proven
Risks mixing audit output with outcome data

rationale: Choose canonical docs plus example artifacts now because M0 should freeze semantics and readiness without running expensive or confounded experiments.

preMortem.scenario: The story accidentally starts Phase 1 data collection.
preMortem.trigger: A maintainer treats cell-manifest examples as active assignments.
preMortem.consequence: Research spend starts before budget lock and runner semantics are ready.
preMortem.mitigation: Label all artifacts as examples and keep README checks provider-free.

preMortem.scenario: Codex CLI is mistaken for an E2 model family.
preMortem.trigger: A reader uses hostKind instead of executorSnapshot for classification.
preMortem.consequence: Multi-model evidence becomes invalid because host and model are conflated.
preMortem.mitigation: Protocol and runner registry must state that snapshots determine E1/E2 classification.

preMortem.scenario: A2 prime cells are considered valid before budget lock.
preMortem.trigger: A manifest includes A2 prime rows without budgetLockDigest.
preMortem.consequence: A2 prime comparison can be post-hoc budgeted and becomes non-admissible.
preMortem.mitigation: Examples and README checks require phase1-budget-lock before A2 prime cells.

preMortem.scenario: Research evidence leaks into product runtime policy.
preMortem.trigger: M6 wording or README implies results should change gates/playbooks automatically.
preMortem.consequence: Proofbound product behavior changes without lineage/exposure/outcome process.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep explicit research-only boundary and require a separate story for product policy changes.
